#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Beads (bd) installation script
# Usage: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/beads/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
#
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This script must be EXECUTED, never SOURCED
# ❌ WRONG: source install.sh (will exit your shell on errors)
# ✅ CORRECT: bash install.sh
# ✅ CORRECT: curl -fsSL ... | bash
#

set -e

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'

    esac
}

sha256_file() {
    local file_path=$1

    if command -v sha256sum &> /dev/null; then
        sha256sum "$file_path" | awk '{print $1}'
        return 0
    fi

    if command -v shasum &> /dev/null; then
        shasum -a 256 "$file_path" | awk '{print $1}'
        return 0
    fi

    if command -v openssl &> /dev/null; then
        openssl dgst -sha256 "$file_path" | awk '{print $2}'
        return 0
    fi

    return 1
}

verify_release_checksum() {
    local release_json=$1
    local version=$2
    local archive_name=$3
    local archive_path=$4

    local checksums_name="checksums.txt"
    local checksums_url="https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/download/${version}/${checksums_name}"

    if ! release_has_asset "$release_json" "$checksums_name"; then
        log_error "Release metadata is missing ${checksums_name}; refusing to install unverified binary"
        return 1
    fi

    if ! download_file "$checksums_url" "$checksums_name"; then
        log_error "Failed to download ${checksums_name}; refusing to install unverified binary"
        return 1
    fi

    local expected
    expected=$(awk -v target="$archive_name" '{name=$2; sub(/^\*/, "", name); if (name == target) {print $1; exit}}' "$checksums_name")
    if [ -z "$expected" ]; then
        log_error "No checksum entry found for ${archive_name} in ${checksums_name}"
        return 1
    fi

    local actual
    actual=$(sha256_file "$archive_path") || {
        log_error "No SHA256 tool found (need one of: sha256sum, shasum, openssl)"
        return 1
    }

    if [ "$expected" != "$actual" ]; then
        log_error "Checksum mismatch for ${archive_name}; refusing to install"
        return 1
    fi

    log_success "Checksum verified for ${archive_name}"
    return 0
}

find_extracted_bd() {
    local search_dir=$1

    if [ -x "$search_dir/bd" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$search_dir/bd"
        return 0
    fi

    local extracted_bd
    extracted_bd=$(find "$search_dir" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -type f -name bd | head -n 1)
    if [ -n "$extracted_bd" ] && [ -x "$extracted_bd" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$extracted_bd"
        return 0
    fi

    return 1
}

# Re-sign binary for macOS only when explicitly requested.
# This replaces the upstream signature with a local ad-hoc signature.
resign_for_macos() {
    local binary_path=$1

    # Only run on macOS
    if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Keep re-signing opt-in so users can decide whether to preserve
    # the release signature/Gatekeeper behavior.
    if [ "${BEADS_INSTALL_RESIGN_MACOS:-0}" != "1" ]; then
        log_info "Skipping macOS ad-hoc re-signing (default)"
        log_info "Set BEADS_INSTALL_RESIGN_MACOS=1 to opt in"
        return 0
    fi

    # Check if codesign is available
    if ! command -v codesign &> /dev/null; then
        log_warning "codesign not found, skipping re-signing"
        return 0
    fi

    log_warning "Opt-in macOS re-sign enabled: replacing release signature with local ad-hoc signature"
    codesign --remove-signature "$binary_path" 2>/dev/null || true
    if codesign --force --sign - "$binary_path"; then
        log_success "Binary re-signed for this machine"
    else
        log_warning "Failed to re-sign binary (non-fatal)"
    fi
}

1041	-- .snapshot()/.clear()/.salvage(): accepted segment text lives only in memory
1042	--   (PL.results) until pipelineFinalize() inserts it. If finalization never
1043	--   runs (stop path aborts, insert throws, or Hammerspoon reloads mid-run) that
1044	--   text would be lost. So we snapshot accepted segments to disk as they
1045	--   complete, clear the snapshot once text is safely inserted, and salvage any
1046	--   orphaned snapshot (on next recording start or on reload) into recent
1047	--   dictations so it can be retrieved from the menu bar.
1048	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1049	_whisperRecovery = { file = WHISPER_TMP .. "/last-session-recovery.txt" }
1050	
1051	function _whisperRecovery.play(path)
1052	    pcall(function()
1053	        local snd = hs.sound.getByFile(path)
1054	        if snd then snd:play() end
1055	    end)
1056	end
1057	
1058	function _whisperRecovery.snapshot()
1059	    local parts = {}
1060	    for n = 1, (PL.nextSeg - 1) do
1061	        local t = PL.results[n]
1062	        if t and t ~= "" then table.insert(parts, t) end
1063	    end
1064	    if #parts == 0 then return end
1065	    local text = table.concat(parts, " "):gsub("%s+", " ")
1066	    local f = io.open(_whisperRecovery.file, "w")
1067	    if f then f:write(text); f:close() end
1068	end
1069	
1070	function _whisperRecovery.clear()
1071	    os.remove(_whisperRecovery.file)
1072	end
1073	
1074	function _whisperRecovery.salvage()
1075	    local f = io.open(_whisperRecovery.file, "r")
1076	    if not f then return end
1077	    local text = f:read("*a"); f:close()
1078	    text = (text or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")
1079	    if text ~= "" then
1080	        log("recovery: salvaged orphaned session text (" .. #text .. " chars) → recent dictations")
1081	        table.insert(recentDictations, 1, {
1082	            text = text,
1083	            time = os.time(),
1084	            inserted = false,
1085	            app = "[recovered]",
1086	        })
1087	        while #recentDictations > 10 do table.remove(recentDictations) end
1088	        saveRecentDictations()
1089	    end
1090	    os.remove(_whisperRecovery.file)
1091	end

1093	-- On load: recover any text stranded by a previous crash/freeze/reload.

1	# local-whisper — Agent Guidelines
2	
3	## Project overview
4	
5	local-whisper is a fully-local macOS dictation tool. Hold a modifier key to record, release to transcribe and insert text at cursor. Powered by whisper.cpp (C/C++, no Python) and Hammerspoon.
6	
7	## Architecture
8	
9	```
10	Hammerspoon eventtap (modifier key hold/release)
11	  → ffmpeg (chunked WAV recording, 1s segments)
12	  → whisper-cli (transcription — tiny model for partials, chosen model for final)
13	  → Post-processing (filler removal, app-aware capitalize)
14	  → Action hooks (voice commands, note-taking, app launching)
15	  → Text insertion at cursor (paste or keystroke)
16	  → Overlay + menu bar updates
17	```
18	
19	Everything runs inside `~/.hammerspoon/init.lua` — no external bash scripts at runtime.
20	
21	## Key paths
22	
23	- `~/.hammerspoon/init.lua` — main config (overlay, recording, insertion, hotkeys, menu bar)
24	- `~/.hammerspoon/local_whisper_actions.lua` — user voice commands (optional, auto-reloads)
25	- `~/.local-whisper/` — all user settings (lang, model, output, prompt, recent dictations)
26	- `~/whisper.cpp/build/bin/whisper-cli` — transcription binary
27	- `~/whisper.cpp/models/` — whisper models (medium, tiny, etc.)

29	- `$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/chunks/` — recording segments (ephemeral)
30	- `$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/whisper-dictate.log` — debug log
31	
32	## Conventions
33	
34	- Single-file architecture: all runtime logic in init.lua
35	- Hammerspoon API: `hs.canvas` for overlay, `hs.eventtap` for key detection and typing, `hs.pasteboard` for paste mode, `hs.task` for async processes, `hs.menubar` for status icon
36	- whisper.cpp binary is `whisper-cli`, NOT `main`
37	- No Python anywhere — this is a pure C/Lua stack
38	- Log to `$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/whisper-dictate.log` for debugging

40	## Testing & debugging
41	
42	### Slash commands
43	- `/debug` — check logs, config state, Ollama status, and recent errors
44	- `/test-refine` — run the LLM refinement eval suite
45	
46	### Reading logs
47	```bash
48	TMPDIR_REAL=$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR) && tail -30 "${TMPDIR_REAL}whisper-dictate/whisper-dictate.log"
49	```

52	### Testing Ollama refinement without dictating
53	```bash
54	curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
55	  -d '{"model":"gemma3:4b","prompt":"<prompt>\n\n<test input>","stream":false}' \
56	  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['response'])"
57	```
58	This lets you iterate on prompt wording without reloading Hammerspoon or dictating.
59

61	```bash
62	./tests/test_refine.sh
63	```
64	Tests filler removal, list formatting, preamble prevention, and content preservation.
65	
66	### Common debug patterns
67	- **Refine not working**: Check `refine: failed` in logs — common causes: Ollama not running, wrong model name, missing `$HOME` env
68	- **Voice commands not matching**: Check `final (auto/...)` log line — whisper may have transcribed differently than expected
69	- **X button not closing overlay**: `hs.canvas:delete()` inside its own mouse callback is silently ignored — must use `canvas:hide()` immediately then defer deletion with `hs.timer.doAfter(0.01, ...)`
70	- **Recent dictations not persisting**: Lua upvalue scoping — never reassign a table variable that closures reference; populate in-place instead
71	
72	### Hammerspoon canvas gotchas
73	- Cannot delete a canvas from within its own mouse callback — defer with `hs.timer.doAfter(0.01, ...)`
74	- Elements at higher indices render on top and intercept mouse events even when invisible (alpha=0)
75	- `hs.task` spawns with minimal environment — always set `HOME` and `PATH` via `task:setEnvironment()`
76	- `img:template(true)` on a menu bar icon lets macOS auto-color for light/dark mode; `template(false)` preserves actual colors
77

80	- Transcribed text is data, not code — never execute it
81	- No network calls — everything stays local
82	- Clipboard contents are overwritten during paste mode
83	- Temp files in $TMPDIR are per-user private on macOS

94	## Issue Tracking with bd (beads)
95	
96	**IMPORTANT**: This project uses **bd (beads)** for ALL issue tracking. Do NOT use markdown TODOs, task lists, or other tracking methods.
97	
98	### Why bd?
99	
100	- Dependency-aware: Track blockers and relationships between issues
101	- Git-friendly: Auto-syncs to JSONL for version control
102	- Agent-optimized: JSON output, ready work detection, discovered-from links
103	- Prevents duplicate tracking systems and confusion
104	
105	### Quick Start
106	
107	**Check for ready work:**
108	
109	```bash
110	bd ready --json
111	```
112	
113	**Create new issues:**
114	
115	```bash
116	bd create "Issue title" --description="Detailed context" -t bug|feature|task -p 0-4 --json
117	bd create "Issue title" --description="What this issue is about" -p 1 --deps discovered-from:bd-123 --json
118	```
119	
120	**Claim and update:**
121	
122	```bash
123	bd update bd-42 --status in_progress --json
124	bd update bd-42 --priority 1 --json
125	```
126	
127	**Complete work:**
128	
129	```bash
130	bd close bd-42 --reason "Completed" --json
131	```
132	
133	### Issue Types
134	
135	- `bug` - Something broken
136	- `feature` - New functionality
137	- `task` - Work item (tests, docs, refactoring)
138	- `epic` - Large feature with subtasks
139	- `chore` - Maintenance (dependencies, tooling)
140	
141	### Priorities
142	
143	- `0` - Critical (security, data loss, broken builds)
144	- `1` - High (major features, important bugs)
145	- `2` - Medium (default, nice-to-have)
146	- `3` - Low (polish, optimization)
147	- `4` - Backlog (future ideas)
148	
149	### Workflow for AI Agents
150	
151	1. **Check ready work**: `bd ready` shows unblocked issues
152	2. **Claim your task**: `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
153	3. **Work on it**: Implement, test, document
154	4. **Discover new work?** Create linked issue:
155	   - `bd create "Found bug" --description="Details about what was found" -p 1 --deps discovered-from:<parent-id>`
156	5. **Complete**: `bd close <id> --reason "Done"`
157	
158	### Auto-Sync
159	
160	bd automatically syncs with git:
161	
162	- Exports to `.beads/issues.jsonl` after changes (5s debounce)
163	- Imports from JSONL when newer (e.g., after `git pull`)
164	- No manual export/import needed!
165	
166	### Important Rules
167	
168	- Use bd for ALL task tracking
169	- Always use `--json` flag for programmatic use
170	- Link discovered work with `discovered-from` dependencies
171	- Check `bd ready` before asking "what should I work on?"
172	- Do NOT create markdown TODO lists

174	- Do NOT duplicate tracking systems

181

183	
184	**MANDATORY WORKFLOW:**
185	
186	1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create issues for anything that needs follow-up
187	2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
188	3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
189	4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
190	   ```bash
191	   git pull --rebase
192	   bd sync
193	   git push
194	   git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
195	   ```
196	5. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
197	6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
198	7. **Hand off** - Provide context for next session
199	
200	**CRITICAL RULES:**
201	- Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds
202	- NEVER stop before pushing - that leaves work stranded locally
203	- NEVER say "ready to push when you are" - YOU must push
